meta.title: Farm Quiz Game — Production & Unlock Tree
meta.status: Draft. Every number is a first-pass guess meant to be tuned with the explorer's pacing check.

units.step: 1 correctly answered Time Quiz question (the game's clock)
units.energy: ⚡ spent by the player (restored by Rest: sleep, food, a sip of water)

pacing.note: Real time = Time Quiz answers × secondsPerStep + actions × secondsPerAction + Rest answers × secondsPerRest + knowledge questions × secondsPerKnowledgeQuestion. Rest answers = energy spent ÷ energy per answer (home, bed, pillow, bottle…).

weeds.note: Weeds grow on every field patch every question, planted or not: ratePerQuestion × weed tier of the chapter × (1 + fertilizerFactor × fertilizer points the patch density needs) × weed multipliers (edging, borders, geese, goat, mulch…). One weeding tap clears weedsPerPull weeds; each weed costs 1 energy (less with hoes) and gives 1 fiber. Orchard spots grow half as many. The first freeDensity plants per patch need no fertilizer; each plant beyond needs 1 fertilizer point per planting.
weeds.diminishing: Weeding has no floor: you can always 'Root out the weeds' (a polish) — the first time cuts regrowth most, every next time half as much and costs more energy, because the last weeds are harder to find.

targets.note: Difficulty should stay steady rather than hit fixed hours: minutes per main goal rise gently (minutesPerGoal), Rest answers per hour stay in a band, and at every moment 2–12 goals are open with a quick win nearby. Pet hours are reported, not forced.

rules: requires = must already be built/unlocked (shown with a lock icon until then). cost = used up once.
replaces = upgrade path; the old tier is consumed and anything that required it is still satisfied.
keeps = needed in the pantry but not used up (tin pot, starter, cultures, the stone in Stone Soup).
tag:x in inputs = any item with that tag (e.g. any vegetable).
Stations with time > 0 work over several questions; slots = batches at once.

Crops: yields per plant. Patch levels (type patch, perPatch) set how many plants of the same crop fit in one patch; plants beyond 2 need fertilizer points every planting (ash 1, compost 2, worm castings 4).

cost.energy = effort for one build or delivery; perPatch costs are paid once per field patch. cat = energy category (field, weed, gather, wood, build, craft, smith, kiln, cook, prep, mill, process, textile, animal).

effects.mult: energy:<cat>, water:field|animal, weeds, grow, feed:<animal>, out:<animal|station>, in:<station>:<item>, time:<station>. Multipliers from different things multiply; an upgrade that replaces another drops the old one's effect.
type helper = optional upgrade that only makes things cheaper. type sidequest = optional favour; the reward is a picture.

type knowledge = a card: requires its book (+ earlier cards), discover = items the player must have held once, cost.read = Time Quiz questions of reading, then a short quiz. unlocks = what lists it in requires.
type book = bought once from the Book Cart (coins); the library level limits how many books fit (bookSlots). requiresCards = number of cards learned.
type gear = clothing & kit worn by the farmer (slots feet, hands, back, bottle, head, apron, pillow, bed); each slot's ladder replaces the previous item.
type polish = endless optional upgrade with diminishing returns (see meta.polish). attach = choice slot on a station: only one item per station is active, swap freely.

New effect keys: scare / pestBlock (pests), fuel and fuel:<station>, muck and muck:<animal>, stones, pests, read, yield:orchard, slots:<station> (add), wear, shelfLife, restedSoil, winterGrow, woodpileCap, homeFuel, bookSlots, luck, luckDuration, energyPerRest.
recipe.fuel = woodpile points per batch. item.buff = eating it makes energy costs ×energy for the next 'questions' Time Quiz questions.

numbers.rule: Every amount is kept exactly in the background (decimals allowed). The player only sees whole numbers: stocks are rounded DOWN, costs and requirements rounded UP, so what looks affordable always is. Percentages from upgrades multiply exactly.

rest.name: Rest
rest.note: Sleep, food and a sip of water. Each correct arithmetic answer restores energy per Rest answer (home + bed + pillow + bottle + library chair + gift cards + polish). A wrong answer restores nothing; no timer. In winter with an empty woodpile the house is cold: Rest gives 25% less.

quiz.note: Time Quiz questions come from the parent's question packs; knowledgeReviewShare of them (0–1, a setting) are due reviews of knowledge cards the child already learned (spaced repetition). 0 turns reviews off.

knowledge.note: To learn a card: own its book, have discovered its items (if any), read it (cost.read = Time Quiz questions of reading, faster with library levels), then answer its quiz: newQuestions about the card + up to maxReviewQuestions from cards it builds on (weakest or longest-unseen first; one per card). Wrong answers can be retried; only first-try answers move a card up a Leitner box. A missed review never blocks — that card just comes back sooner. Cards unlock things (anything that lists them in requires), give a permanent boost (effects), or both.

autumn.abundance: Fruit and nuts: orchard +40%; branches fall (sticks ×2).

winter.abundance: Frost brings stones up (pick them for walls); indoor work by the fire −10% energy; wool grows thick.

seasons.note: Seasons only change speeds and amounts — nothing dies. Crops just grow slower in winter (the greenhouse doesn't care). The season shows how many questions are left until the next one.

freshness.rule: At each change of season, food that has already lived through shelfLife season changes turns stale: plant food becomes Feed Mash, eggs and dairy go to the Compost pile. A 'stale soon' badge shows on anything that will turn at the next change — sell it, eat it, or cook it into something that keeps.
freshness.note: Cellar Racks add 1 season to everything; the Cool Cellar card adds 1 more. Preserved goods never spoil: flour, honey, jam, pickles, aged cheese, oils, cider, vinegar, grains, seeds, nuts.

water.note: Water never comes by itself: every drop is carried. A trip with the old bucket brings fetchBase 💧 for fetchEnergy ⚡ (gathering upgrades make it cheaper). Wells, the yoke, the dug-out pond and more make each trip bring more and the store hold more, so later on you carry water less often. Rain waters the fields: planting costs no water until the next question.

pests.note: Every question, pests arrive in proportion to the plants growing (ratePerPlant × plants × chapter tier × season × (1 − fence block)). The scarecrow (and cat, owl, ducks) chases up to 'scare' pests away per question and leaveRate of the rest wander off. The pests that stay eat a share of every growing patch: eatPerPest × pests (at most maxEat), worked out exactly every question and shown rounded to a whole percent; a patch never drops below 1 plant. All this happens once per question; the map plays it when the farm is seen again after the Time Quiz: the scarecrow throws as many angry looks at once as its level (1–4), then the pests that stayed come one by one, eat a plant and carry it off, and come back a few seconds later.

stones.note: In winter, frost lifts stones in every field patch (more in deep beds and bare beds). Stones slow growth a little (like weeds, together at most 50%). Picking them gives stones for walls, paths and buildings.

fuel.note: Heat stations take recipe.fuel points from the woodpile per batch (campfire 1, stove 1, oven 2, kiln 3, forge 2…). The home burns homeFuel per question in winter (tent 0.2 → farmhouse 0.4; the hearth −30%). Stack wood onto the woodpile any time; the woodpile holds woodpileCap points (basket 20, shed 40, warehouse 80).

muck.note: Each collection leaves muck (hens 0.3, cows 1, sheep 0.6 per animal). Above thresholdPerAnimal × animals the animals give 25% less; above twice that, 50% less. Mucking out costs energyPerMuck per muck and gives manure (compost!).

rotation.note: A patch remembers its last crop. The same crop again grows 15% slower (tired soil); after beans or clover the next crop grows 10% faster (rested soil).

polish.note: Polish = endless optional upgrades (sharpen, oil, clean, re-stuff, air…). Each polish adds 1 point P. The effect listed is the cap: the first point gives half of it, the second a quarter more, the third an eighth… while the cost rises by the base every time. Use (or time) wears P down slowly (wear), so it's also maintenance. New KINDS of upgrade are always worth more than grinding the same one.

luck.note: A hidden background number (starts at 0) that makes lucky things a bit more likely: chance × (1 + luck). Side quests give +0.5 for 30 questions, Little Jobs +0.1 for 10, a four-leaf clover +0.3 for 20; each pet adds +0.05 for good; the Lucky Horseshoe gift card +0.15 for good.

events.text: A lost coin in the weeds!
A four-leaf clover! You feel lucky.
Something old in the soil: a relic for the album!
A sparkling quartz crystal inside a stone!
It rained: no watering needed, and the well fills a little.

giftCards.note: Gifts that help on the farm. They come on postcards from friends (meta.postcards) and cannot be bought. Only maxActive gifts work at the same time; the others wait in the album and can be swapped in.

jobs.note: Three small jobs that refill themselves as soon as one is done (only things the player can do right now). Reward: a few coins and a little luck.

practice.note: Every station counts how often it was used. At 10, 40 and 120 uses it earns a star: −5% energy for its recipes per star.

acorns.note: Seven Golden Acorns hide in the game, each found a different way. Each one raises the energy max by 3 for good.

meta.note_on_numbers: Costs per chapter were scaled by the pacing check so the minutes per main goal rise gently (meta.targets.minutesPerGoal); change any number and re-check it in progression-explorer.html (drop this file onto the page).

yield.note: Crop yields are averages per plant. Each plant gives its average × (1 + luck × luckShift) × the patch's quality, plus a random spread (spread × average), rounded up or down at random so the average is kept. The first item of a crop is at least minMain per plant. Upgrades raise the average (yield_<item> adds to every harvest).

building.note: Big buildings are built in steps (node.steps): each step takes its own materials and some energy, and the next step can only start after 'wait' Time Quiz questions (the mortar dries, the wood settles). node.cost is the total.

market.note: Each thing sells at full price for the first fullPrice units; every further unit of the same thing fetches dropPerUnit less (down to floor). Every Time Quiz question the market forgets recoverShare of what was sold lately (at least recoverPerQuestion units). Selling many different things pays best; a big pile of one thing sold at once pays a little less.

pricing.note: How made things are priced (tools/econ check): worth of the inputs x (inputsMult + perDifferentInput x (different inputs - 1)) + perEnergy x energy + perFuel x fuel + perWater x water + perQuestion x station time. A dish of four different things pays more than its parts; a dish made from dishes pays more again.

perks.note: Small extras that make the farm prettier or livelier. They do not change the economy. Some come from favours (side quest 'perk'), others from achievements ('when': rest_quick>=N quick Rest answers, medals>=N Rest sum medals won, sold_kinds>=N different things sold, harvests>=N, seasons>=N, cards>=N, sidequests>=N, unlocked:id). Every perk can be switched off in the album.

postcards.note: Friends are the people you helped (finished side quests; the same person counts once). At a milestone (a pet arrives, the library grows, every 12 goals) a friend may hear of it and send a postcard with a gift: chance = chanceBase + chancePerFriend x friends (at most 100%; the very first postcard always comes). The gift is picked from as many cards as there are friends (1, 2, 3 at most). Cards not picked can come again on a later postcard.

carry.note: Carrying gear (effect add.carry) makes a gathering tap take 1 + carry loads at once: outputs and energy both grow with it, so the energy per piece stays the same, but more comes in per question (each spot refills once per question). A tap takes a smaller load when energy is short.

flex.note: Dynamic difficulty (settings dynamicDifficulty, or ⚙️ Settings → Prices fit my farm). pace = worth of what the player brings in per Time Quiz question (running average over paceQuestions; things bought don't count; things worth nothing count minWorth). basePace = the pace the test bot has after so many goals ([goals done, pace], a straight line in between; tests/bot.gd prints pace_sample lines). When a goal of these types first shows up while open, factor = (pace / basePace) ^ strength, × (1 + tipBonus) if an improvement not made yet would make it quicker, kept within range (rangeSide for favours); it is then fixed for that goal. Coins and material amounts of 2 or more are multiplied (never beyond what the store holds); energy and the kinds of things never change. No factor before warmup questions. The pace also grows when a player simply works more per question, so only part of it is followed (strength 0.4) and the range is narrow.

chapters.theme: Timber & clay. Kitchen, cows, bees, bread — and iron ore at the end.

chapters.name: Smallholding
chapters.theme: Iron. Double harvests, sheep & cloth, windmill, press, cellar.

chapters.name: Village Trade
chapters.theme: Steel & glass. Farmhouse, greenhouse, orchard oils, pizza.

chapters.name: Master Farm
chapters.theme: Heirlooms, saffron, plant dyes and colour mixing, master baking.

stick.name: Stick
stick.desc: From clearing bushes and the Woodlot.

stone.name: Stone
stone.desc: From clearing rocky patches; cheap at the Raw Materials Merchant.

fiber.name: Plant Fiber
fiber.desc: Tough weed stems. Twisted into rope; compostable.

rope.name: Rope
rope.desc: 3 fiber twisted together. Ties every early build.

straw.name: Straw
straw.desc: By-product of wheat and oats. Thatch, bedding, compost, beehive skeps. Nobody buys straw — use it.

log.name: Log
log.desc: From stumps, the Woodlot and later the Lumbermill.

plank.name: Plank
plank.desc: Split from logs (axe) — four times as many with a saw.

clay.name: Clay
clay.desc: Bought, or dug at the Pond.

brick.name: Brick
brick.desc: Fired clay. Ovens, kilns, forges, the Farmhouse.

charcoal.name: Charcoal
charcoal.desc: Slow-burnt logs. Fuel for forge and glass kiln.

iron_ore.name: Iron Ore
iron_ore.desc: Only from the Raw Materials Merchant (unlocked by a dish).

iron.name: Iron Bar
iron.desc: Smelted ore. The iron age starts here.

nails.name: Nails
nails.desc: 1 iron bar → 4 nails. Every serious wooden build needs them.

steel.name: Steel Bar
steel.desc: Iron refined with lots of charcoal. Top-tier tools and machines.

glass.name: Glass
glass.desc: Windows for the Farmhouse, panes for the Greenhouse.

hardwood.name: Hardwood
hardwood.desc: Dense oak for machine parts. Bought, later grown at the Lumbermill.

clay_jar.name: Clay Jar
clay_jar.desc: Fired clay jar. Pickles, jam, olives and the fermenter need them.

ash.name: Wood Ash
ash.desc: Burnt weeds and twigs. The first fertilizer: worth 1 point.

compost.name: Compost
compost.desc: Worth 2 fertilizer points. Hungry crops need 1 compost each. Made from straw/weeds, much faster with manure.

worm_castings.name: Worm Castings
worm_castings.desc: Worth 4 fertilizer points. Worms turn compost and straw into the richest soil.

manure.name: Manure
manure.desc: From cows and sheep. Makes compost much faster.

oilcake.name: Oilcake
oilcake.desc: Left over after pressing sunflower seeds. Animal feed or compost.

tin_pot.name: Tin Pot
tin_pot.desc: The one thing that survived. Needed (not used up) for campfire cooking.

sourdough_starter.name: Sourdough Starter
sourdough_starter.desc: Made once, never used up: bread needs it present.

yogurt_culture.name: Yogurt Culture
yogurt_culture.desc: Bought once from the Culture Specialist; kept alive by every batch.

cheese_culture.name: Cheese Culture
cheese_culture.desc: Bought once from the Culture Specialist (plant-based rennet).

saffron_corm.name: Saffron Corm
saffron_corm.desc: Rare seed, bartered from the Import Broker.

rainbow_carrot_seed.name: Rainbow Carrot Seeds
rainbow_carrot_seed.desc: Rare seed, bartered from the Import Broker.

golden_beet_seed.name: Golden Beet Seeds
golden_beet_seed.desc: Rare seed, bartered from the Import Broker.

woad_seed.name: Woad Seeds
woad_seed.desc: Rare seed, bartered from the Import Broker.

feather.name: Feather
feather.desc: Hens drop them. Pillows, the library feather duster, the scarecrow's hat.

feed_mash.name: Feed Mash
feed_mash.desc: Old vegetables chopped with straw — or food that went stale at the change of season. Hens, cows and sheep eat it; the compost takes it too.

linseed.name: Linseed
linseed.desc: Flax seeds. Pressed for linseed oil, or fed to hens.

linseed_oil.name: Linseed Oil
linseed_oil.desc: Oils tools, looms and wood. (Not for frying.)

quartz.name: Quartz Crystal
quartz.desc: Sometimes hiding in a stone. Pretty, and the market pays well.

relic.name: Old Relic
relic.desc: An arrowhead, an old coin, a fossil… found while weeding. Goes in the album, or sell it.

honey_cake.name: Honey Cake
honey_cake.desc: A cake sweetened with honey instead of sugar.

tent.name: Tent
tent.desc: Where it starts. Energy max 20; each Rest answer gives 5 energy.

well_1.name: Old Bucket
well_1.desc: All that is left: a small dented bucket. Carry water from the wild pond: 2 💧 a trip for 1 ⚡. Holds 8.

ruins_workshop.name: Clear the old workshop
ruins_workshop.desc: What is left of the old workshop is in the way: clear it away before anything new can stand here. It gives stones back.

ruins_lumber.name: Clear the burnt woodshed
ruins_lumber.desc: What is left of the burnt woodshed is in the way: clear it away before anything new can stand here. It gives sticks, charcoal and ash back.

ruins_barn.name: Clear the burnt barn
ruins_barn.desc: What is left of the burnt barn is in the way: clear it away before anything new can stand here. It gives sticks, charcoal and ash back.

ruins_compost.name: Clear the old compost corner
ruins_compost.desc: What is left of the old compost corner is in the way: clear it away before anything new can stand here. It gives sticks, charcoal and ash back.

ruins_windmill.name: Clear the old mill
ruins_windmill.desc: What is left of the old mill is in the way: clear it away before anything new can stand here. It gives stones back.

ruins_greenhouse.name: Clear the old glasshouse
ruins_greenhouse.desc: What is left of the old glasshouse is in the way: clear it away before anything new can stand here. It gives stones back.

road_1.name: Muddy track
road_1.desc: The old road is mud and potholes. Only the seed seller with her basket gets through.

road_1b.name: Lay brushwood over the mud
road_1b.desc: Bundles of brushwood over the worst mud: the seed seller's handcart gets through a little more often.

road_2.name: Fill the potholes
road_2.desc: Stones and sticks in the worst holes: carts can come now — the timber & stone seller, the seed cart and the book cart.

road_2b.name: Dig a ditch for the puddles
road_2b.desc: A ditch along the road drains the puddles: the bean grower's cart can come now.

road_3.name: Gravel road
road_3.desc: A firm gravel road: heavy carts with clay and iron ore can reach your farm, and the seed shop delivers.

road_3b.name: Edge the road with kerbstones
road_3b.desc: Kerbstones keep the gravel in place: the sunflower seller from the hills dares the trip.

road_4.name: Cobbled road
road_4.desc: Cobbles and a ditch: the hardwood & sand carts and the nursery come even after rain.

road_4b.name: Plant trees along the road
road_4b.desc: A row of young trees gives shade and shelter: the herb woman walks over from the next valley.

road_5.name: Paved road & bridge
road_5.desc: A paved road with a stone bridge: guild wagons and travellers from far away find your farm.

basket.name: Basket
basket.desc: Holds up to 10 of each item.

hands.name: Hands
hands.desc: Plant, harvest and pull weeds by hand.

rock.name: Rock
rock.desc: Good enough to knock simple things together.

bucket.name: Watering Scoop
bucket.desc: Waters the plants. Plants use their full water cost.

seed_1.name: Seed Merchant
seed_1.desc: Always there, always takes coins. Wheat and carrot seeds.

land_start.name: One cleared patch
land_start.desc: The rest of the field is overgrown.

crop_wheat.name: Wheat
crop_wheat.desc: The backbone crop: food, feed, flour and straw.

campfire.name: Campfire
campfire.desc: First build. With the Tin Pot: porridge and soup.

d_porridge.name: Feed the travelling merchant
d_porridge.desc: She shares news — and opens her cart properly.

raw_1.name: Raw Materials · timber & stone
raw_1.desc: Safety valve for basic building materials.

crop_clover.name: Clover
crop_clover.desc: Cheap, quick fodder. Its flowers feed bees.

present_onion.name: A present for the seed cart
present_onion.desc: Give the seed seller two bowls of porridge — next time she brings onion sets.

clear_thistles.name: Clear the thistles (2 patches)
clear_thistles.desc: Takes 4 steps, one tap each; every step gives something back. After the first 2 steps the 2 patches can be planted; the other steps make them better (bigger harvests, fewer weeds).

clear_weeds.name: Pull the weeds (2 patches)
clear_weeds.desc: Takes 5 steps, one tap each; every step gives something back. After the first 2 steps the 2 patches can be planted; the other steps make them better (bigger harvests, fewer weeds).

stone_knife.name: Stone Knife
stone_knife.desc: Rough chopping. Needed for any recipe that cuts things.

stone_axe.name: Hand Axe
stone_axe.desc: Clears stumps, splits logs into planks, cuts sticks faster.

wooden_shovel.name: Wooden Shovel
wooden_shovel.desc: Pries out rocks and digs beds: field work −10% energy.

clear_rocks.name: Clear the rocks (2 patches)
clear_rocks.desc: Takes 5 steps, one tap each; every step gives something back. After the first 2 steps the 2 patches can be planted; the other steps make them better (bigger harvests, fewer weeds).

clear_stumps.name: Clear the stumps (2 patches)
clear_stumps.desc: Takes 5 steps, one tap each; every step gives something back. After the first 2 steps the 2 patches can be planted; the other steps make them better (bigger harvests, fewer weeds).

chopping_block.name: Chopping Block
chopping_block.desc: A stump to cut on. Salads and bowls (needs a knife).

quern.name: Hand Quern
quern.desc: Two flat stones from the rocky patch grind wheat into flour. Hard work (2 ⚡).

well_2.name: Dig a well
well_2.desc: A stone well right by the house: 4 💧 a trip, holds 24.

well_3.name: Well · winch
well_3.desc: A winch and a bigger bucket: 6 💧 a trip, holds 36.

animal_chicken.name: Chickens
animal_chicken.desc: Eat any grain (wheat, oats, sunflower seeds, linseed, mash), need water and nest straw, lay an egg every question — and drop a feather now and then.

scarecrow_1.name: Stick Scarecrow
scarecrow_1.desc: Shoots fierce looks at birds and rabbits (removes 0.6 pests per question) and they leave the seeds alone: planting costs half the energy.

d_veg_soup.name: Soup for the village

seed_3.name: Seed Merchant · stall

spice_1.name: Spice Merchant
spice_1.desc: Salt. (Barter idea: also asks for 1 onion per salt.)

compost_bin.name: Compost Bin
compost_bin.desc: Turns straw, fiber and manure into compost over a few questions.

pet_bunny.name: Bunny comes home
pet_bunny.desc: Pet 1 (default name Pip; the player can rename). Bonus: every carrot harvest gives +1 carrot.

cottage_walls.name: Cottage · log walls

cottage.name: Cottage

present_lettuce.name: Soup for the seed stall

present_beet.name: Pancakes for the seed stall
present_beet.desc: A pancake breakfast for the stall keeper — she asks her cousin for beet seed.

crop_tomato.name: Tomato
crop_tomato.desc: Ingredient-threshold unlock (kept from the prototype): bring 2 eggs once. Hungry crop: needs compost.

d_stone_soup.name: Stone Soup for the quarry folk

carpenter_bench.name: Carpenter's Bench

kiln.name: Kiln

prep_table_1.name: Prep Table

woodlot.name: Woodlot
